text:
anya: Heads-up: customer acct-847E reports duplicate billing after reconnects where the client uses HTTP/2 multiplexing. They see a partial chunk on stream 1, then open a second concurrent stream to resume and we end up generating the remainder — appears billed twice. Repro attached.

mohit: Can you paste client lib + exact request flow? HTTP/2 w/ concurrent streams vs separate TCP connections? Any proxies or LB in front?

anya: Node client using http2 wrapper around fetch. Client spawns a second stream immediately when first stream gets a connection reset. Minimal repro from customer described below.

jess: Do we know if they used the resume token or just retried the full prompt?

anya: Logs from their session: \n```\n2026-03-15T14:12:34Z INFO stream-id=abcd chunk=1 status=partial offset=0\n2026-03-15T14:12:36Z WARN stream-id=abcd connection=reset client_stream=1\n2026-03-15T14:12:36Z INFO session=acct-847E new_stream=2 resume_token=rt:123\n2026-03-15T14:12:36Z INFO generation=start stream=2 prompt_len=120\n2026-03-15T14:12:38Z INFO generation=complete tokens=98 billed=true\n```\n
jess: That resume_token looks client generated and sent with the second stream. If stream 1 hadn't fully acknowledged the partial output, runtime may accept stream 2 and start a fresh generation. We should dedupe server-side.

mohit: Current behavior note: our dedupe relies on idempotency_key header; resume_token is advisory and not used for hard dedupe. If a second stream arrives we treat it as a new request. That matches the logs.

kyle: tagging @billing-bot and @eng-runtime. Please hold billing for acct-847E while we investigate — we might owe credits.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0031; severity=P2; assignee=eng-runtime.

dev-runtime: Quick context: for HTTP/2 multiplexing the upstream sees separate stream IDs; our in-flight map keys on connection+stream-id for partials, not on session+resume_token. So a parallel stream looks like a new request.

jess: Proposed mitigations: (1) server-side dedupe that checks session_id + resume_token within a 60s window; (2) write-ahead generation-id persisted before billing event so duplicate starts can be suppressed; (3) short-term: return 409 if resume_token re-used while original stream still in-progress.

anya: Customer wants a reproducible snippet to run locally so they can confirm. Can we provide a minimal client example?

jess: Share this node snippet (pseudo):\n```\n// pseudo client: open two concurrent http2 streams to /v1/streams\nconst http2 = require('http2');\nconst c = http2.connect('https://inference.redwood.ai');\nconst req1 = c.request({':path':'/v1/streams', ':method':'POST','content-type':'application/json'});\n// simulate partial / connection reset\nsetTimeout(()=>{\n  const req2 = c.request({':path':'/v1/streams', ':method':'POST','content-type':'application/json'});\n  // attach same resume_token in body/headers\n}, 100);\n```\n
mohit: Action items: \n- eng-runtime: implement server-side dedupe by (session_id + resume_token + prompt_hash) and persist generation-id before billing.\n- billing: pause/flag acct-847E and queue credit if duplicate tokens confirmed.\n- support: short KB advising clients to avoid parallel reconnect streams; prefer single reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter.

kyle: I'll coordinate with billing and draft customer message offering temporary credit. @billing-bot please pause automated invoices for acct-847E.

billing-bot: Action queued: pause billing for acct-847E pending investigation.

anya: I'll send repro snippet and ask for their client logs + exact timings. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jess: I'll follow up with a runtime PR for generation-id write-ahead + dedupe check; ETA EOD.

mohit: Also check LB/proxy (envoy) behavior — if the client sits behind a proxy that reuses connections or downgrades http2->http1 it could change stream semantics. Good to rule that out.

anya: Adding notes to support doc with next-steps and temporary mitigation message for customers.
